name: nycrc

extends.description: Name of configuration to extend from.

all.description: Whether or not to instrument all files (not just the ones touched by your test suite).

check-coverage.description: Check whether coverage is within thresholds, fail if not

extension.description: List of extensions that nyc should attempt to handle in addition to .js

include.description: List of files to include for coverage.

exclude.description: List of files to exclude for coverage.

reporter.description: The names of custom reporter to show coverage results.

report-dir.description: Where to put the coverage report files.

skip-full.description: Don't show files with 100% statement, branch, and function coverage

temp-dir.description: Directory to output raw coverage information to.

description:
We’re extending the base configuration `@myorg/nyc-config` and have turned on full instrumentation, so every file in the project will be instrumented (`all: true`). Coverage thresholds are being enforced (`check‑coverage: true`), and the tool is set up to recognize a broad range of source extensions: `.js`, `.cjs`, `.mjs`, `.ts`, `.tsx`, `.jsx` and `.json`. The coverage scanner will include all JavaScript and TypeScript files under `src/**/*.js` and `src/**/*.ts`, as well as test files matching `test/**/*.js`, while explicitly excluding the `coverage/**`, `node_modules/**`, and `dist/**` directories.

For reporting, we’ll generate HTML and LCOV files together with a concise text‑summary, all placed in the `./coverage/reports` directory. Files that already have 100 % statement, branch, and function coverage will be omitted from the output (`skip-full: true`). Intermediate raw coverage data will be written to the temporary folder `./.nyc_output`.
